title: justify-content
definition: A flexbox container property that defines how space is distributed between and around content items along the main-axis (horizontal by default).
simpleExplanation: If you have 3 buttons in a row, and a bunch of empty space at the end, what do you do with the space? `justify-content` answers that. You can pack the buttons to the left (`flex-start`), pack them to the right (`flex-end`), center them (`center`), or put equal space between them (`space-between`).
realWorldExample: A Header. You have a Logo on the far left, and a Login button on the far right. You put them in a flex container and use `justify-content: space-between`. They instantly push to opposite sides of the screen.
useCases: Pushing elements to opposite sides of a container

basic: What value pushes items to the far right of the container?
intermediate: What is the difference between `space-between` and `space-around`?

answers.question: space-between vs space-around?
answers.answer: `space-between` pushes the first item flush against the left wall, the last item flush against the right wall, and spaces the rest evenly. `space-around` leaves a gap between the walls and the first/last items.
